title: Homomorphism counting for immersion-closed classes is not isomorphism
summary: Lovász proved that two graphs $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic if $\hom(K,G) = \hom(K,H)$ for all graphs $K$, where $\hom(G_1,G_2)$ denotes the number of homomorphisms from $G_1$ to $G_2$. Dvořák showed that it suffices to count homomorphisms from all $2$-degenerate graphs $K$. On the other hand, for several interesting graph classes $\mathcal{M}$, it has been shown that there exist non-isomorphic graphs $G$ and $H$ such that $\hom(K,G)=\hom(K,H)$ for all $K\in \mathcal{M}$.
